Subject: Praxis MAP: cost breakdown + evaluation plan questions

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we prepare the Mutual Action Plan and internal eval, procurement has asked for a tighter breakdown on the cost model assumptions so our finance team can sign off. Specifically we need: tokens per API call assumptions (avg prompt & completion lengths), any caching or prefix-warmup logic you expect to apply, batching behavior for burst traffic, and expected tokens/$ at pilot scale (10k–50k calls/day).

I've attached our draft MAP (praxis_map_v1.docx) — the timeline pins a 6-week pilot starting 03/29. Can you confirm whether the MAP's numbers align with Redwood's preferred evaluation approach, and highlight any gotchas we should add to our risk section?

Would appreciate a short note today or a 30-min call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Alex

Head of Product, Praxis Health

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 7 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Praxis MAP: cost breakdown + evaluation plan questions

Alex — great to hear from you and thanks for the MAP doc.

Quick summary up front: yes, we can align to your timeline, but the unit economics will hinge on three levers we typically validate during the eval window: (1) average sequence length per interaction (prompt + completion), (2) prefix/KV cache hit rate (how many calls can reuse cached context), and (3) effective batching during short bursts.

Prelim assumptions we propose for the pilot (we'll validate these once we get sample traffic):
- Avg prompt tokens: 120
- Avg completion tokens: 80
- Baseline tokens/request: 200 tokens
- Expected cache hit rate (prefix reuse): 22% (lower if users vary prompts)
- Effective batching: 1.4x tokens-per-sec improvement in burst windows with our continuous-batching defaults

Using those baseline values, rough tokens/$ at pilot scale (NVIDIA A100-backed hosted profile, mixed-quantized model): 0.00045 USD per token -> ~USD 0.09 per request (200 tokens). This is an initial estimate; we'll produce a sketched spreadsheet with sensitivity runs.

I've attached a starter token economics workbook (redwood_token_econ.xlsx) — it contains the sensitivity slider for cache hit rates, batching multipliers, and sequence-length scenarios. I'll also propose a short call Monday to walk the MAP assumptions with your team.

Next steps:
- Mateo to walk through the workbook with Praxis on Mon 03/09 10:30am PT (proposed)
- Praxis to send a 48-hour traffic sample or representative prompt set (privileged)
- Redwood to finalize pilot token assumptions and share updated MAP v1.1

Thanks — looping Neha for procurement alignment and David for ops-level cost verification.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_token_econ.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: david_kim@redwood.ai <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 7 Mar 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Praxis MAP: cost breakdown + evaluation plan questions (ops notes)

Folks — quick ops note to include in the MAP risk section and for the call:

- Model variant: please confirm whether Praxis will evaluate on a medium-size open model (e.g., 13B quantized) or a larger variant. Tokens/$ differ ~2x between these classes once you include kv-cache memory costs and throughput.
- Sequence-length distribution: if 5–10% of calls go >1k tokens, planning numbers change materially. Add a high-tail scenario in the workbook.
- Caching nuance: prefix caching works best when there is a stable conversational prefix or system prompt. If end-users send highly varied prompts, cache hit rate can drop to single-digit %.
- Batching: our continuous-batching yields gains mainly for sub-second bursts; sustained high concurrency should be sized as Dedicated to get predictable throughput.

I'll prepare two quick tabs in redwood_token_econ.xlsx: (A) model-variant compare, (B) high-tail sequence scenario. Mateo — can you confirm the call slot?

-David
David Kim
Lead, Inference Ops, Redwood Inference
